# Negligence

## Negligence

Negligence is a failure to take the care that a reasonable person would take in the same situation. To succeed in a negligence claim, a claimant must show a duty of care, a breach of that duty, and damage caused by the breach. A duty of care exists when harm to the other person was reasonably foreseeable. A breach occurs when the defendant's conduct falls below the standard of a reasonable person.

## Causation and defences

Causation requires that the damage would not have happened but for the defendant's breach. Damage that is too remote or unforeseeable is not recoverable. If the claimant partly caused their own harm, a court may reduce the damages in proportion to their share of the fault. Professionals are judged by the standard of a reasonably competent member of their profession.
